Human motion → Robot motion
Concept illustration, not a live robot feed.

Research / Max Planck Institute

Translating movement
into interaction.

Motion capture pipelines and real-time robot software for human–robot teleoperation.

ROS 2C++Motion capture
Explore the work ＋

The challenge

Connect human pose data to robotic systems within an existing research framework.

My contribution

Led a ROS 1 to ROS 2 migration, rewrote performance-critical components in C++, and refactored motion capture pipelines. Worked with Xsens and Captury data, rotation matrices, robot coordinate systems, RViz, and TF visualization.

Hands-on platforms: Baxter, NAO, and in-house robots.

Vision → Language → Interaction
Hand landmarks / Gesture recognition

Research project / 2023

More ways to
be understood.

A multimodal assistive system connecting sign language recognition, speech, and text.

OpenCVMediaPipeMachine learning
Explore the project ＋

The idea

Bring gesture recognition and speech interfaces into one real-time interaction pipeline.

What I built

Hand landmark detection and gesture segmentation with OpenCV and MediaPipe, curated vision datasets, and a logistic regression classifier for one- and two-handed signs. Integrated speech-to-text and text-to-speech into a low-latency pipeline.

Physical space → Digital twin
Sensors · MQTT · Cloud

IoT project / 2022

A clearer view
of physical space.

A parking validation system that connects sensor data to a cloud-based digital twin.

ESP8266AWS IoTMQTT
Explore the project ＋

The system

ESP8266 microcontrollers and ultrasonic sensors collect occupancy data and stream it through secure MQTT to AWS IoT Core.

What I built

A digital twin model with an EC2-based backend for remote monitoring and predictive insights.

03 / A little about me

Curiosity is
the constant.

From electronics in Pune to information technology in Stuttgart, I keep coming back to one question: how can we make technology easier to interact with?

I’m pursuing an MEng in Information Technology at Universität Stuttgart while working in Haptic Intelligence research. My work brings together software, perception, and physical systems.
